answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks via Proof of Space-Time, anchoring identities to allocated storage. Each agent periodically proves it stores unique datasets, preventing adversaries from running parallel clones on a single compute island. Instead of broadcasting a forged whisper across the network lagoon, attackers incur verifiable hardware and electricity costs per dedicated drive. However, this requirement penalizes lightweight edge agents and fosters storage centralization.
